success_patterns: Verbatim archive hit: the clue's distinctive words appeared in a J!-Archive-style line ('CATEGORY | clue | Oscar Wilde. right: Ted.'). The agent copied the answer that follows the clue and ignored the many noisy 'jury' pages, as Rule 3 directs.

Lyric-quote clue: the lyric string repeated across many passages beside one song title, plus the year and 'hit' detail, gave the title. The agent answered with the bare title, without quotes, album or artist.
Character-name list ('Inspector Luger, Wojo, Fish'): the agent answered with the shared TV series, not one character or actor, as the existing list rule says.
'Lemmon & this actor' clue: the agent treated the named actor as an anchor and answered with the co-star the passages list beside him (Tony Curtis). It did not echo Lemmon or answer with the film.

patch.reasoning: Most of the batch's success came from rules already in the skill: verbatim archive matching, character list to work, and referent-not-anchor. Two small gaps remain. Quoted-lyric clues (the answer is the song title, not the artist or album) are not described. 'A & this <person>' clues, where the answer is the missing co-member of a pair or group, are only covered for generic set members. These two additions are narrow and low-risk. They avoid the broad formatting rewrites that were rejected in earlier steps.

edits.target: and answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content: - Quoted lyric or line clues ('1991 hit that contains the lines "I thought that I heard you laughing..."') ask for the TITLE of the song, poem or speech that contains the quote, not the artist, the album or the lyric itself. Find the passages that repeat the quoted words next to a title (songfacts, lyrics pages, 'Album=... Song Lyrics') and use the year or 'hit' detail to confirm. Give the bare title without quotation marks ('Losing My Religion').

edits.target: asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content: - 'X & this <actor/person>' ('Lemmon & this actor joined an all-girl band', 'Laurel & this comedian'): X is an anchor already given. The answer is the OTHER member of the pair or group. Take the co-star or partner the passages list with X in the same sentence or cast line ('Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon'). Do not repeat X, and do not answer with the film, the character or the group name.
